questions: When performing the operation, can we swap any occurrence of a with any occurrence of b, or only specific ones? The prompt says 'choose an integer pair (i, j) such that A_i = a and A_j = b', which seems to allow any such pair, but is there any restriction on which indices i and j can be chosen (e.g., must they be distinct, or can they be the same index, which would be impossible since a and b are different)?

The operation can be performed 'one or more times'. Does this mean we can perform swaps involving only a and b, or can we also involve other values (like temporarily swapping a with some c) to achieve adjacency? The prompt only mentions swapping a and b directly.

When we say 'reach a state where the two occurrences of a in A are adjacent and the two occurrences of b in A are also adjacent', does adjacency mean immediately next to each other in the sequence (i.e., positions k and k+1), or could they be adjacent after some reordering? The prompt uses 'adjacent' in the usual sense, but is it required that both couples are adjacent simultaneously in the same configuration?

Are we allowed to perform swaps that temporarily break the condition that the two occurrences of a are not adjacent (or b not adjacent) during the process, as long as we end with both adjacent? The initial conditions require non-adjacency, but the process might pass through adjacent states.

Does the operation require swapping exactly one pair per step, or can we swap multiple pairs in one operation? The prompt says 'choose an integer pair (i, j)' and swap them, implying one swap per operation, but 'one or more times' suggests multiple steps.

When counting pairs (a, b), do we consider the order of swaps? That is, if we can achieve adjacency through some sequence of swaps, is that sufficient regardless of the sequence? The prompt says 'it is possible to reach a state', so any sequence should work.
Is the swap operation allowed to swap two elements that are already adjacent in the sequence? The prompt doesn't prohibit it, but does it affect the condition that initially a and b are not adjacent?

What does 'both couples can end up sitting next to each other' mean? Does it require that after the swaps, the two a's are adjacent AND the two b's are adjacent, but also that these two pairs (the a-pair and b-pair) are disjoint? The prompt doesn't specify whether the a-pair and b-pair can overlap (they can't since a ≠ b).
